symptoms.name: throbbing headache
symptoms.description: One-sided, alternating, throbbing headaches localized on forehead, sometimes radiating to neck. Average 13 headache days per month, lasting 12 hours each, severity 9/10

chief_complaint: Chronic debilitating headaches occurring 13 days per month with severe pain (9/10)
history_present_illness: Patient presents with history of chronic migraine since age 22, now experiencing 13 headache days per month. Each episode lasts approximately 12 hours with throbbing, one-sided pain rating 9/10. Current anti-CGRP therapy trial ongoing.
source: PMC10198612 - A case report of a chronic migraine patient treated with three different anti-CGRP monoclonal antibodies (2023)

medical_history: Recurrent neurological episodes for 6 years (onset age 51)
Family history of migraine (grandmother, aunt, cousin)

symptoms.name: visual disturbances
symptoms.description: Flickering in both eyes, recurring episodes

symptoms.name: sensory disturbances
symptoms.description: Unilateral numbness of fingers, left face hypoesthesia

symptoms.name: speech disturbances
symptoms.description: Unable to comprehend or produce words during episodes

symptoms.name: severe headache
symptoms.description: Severe one-sided headache lasting 3-7 days per episode

symptoms.name: hemiparesis
symptoms.description: Weakness on one side of body

chief_complaint: Recurrent episodes of visual disturbances, speech problems, weakness, and severe headaches lasting up to a week, occurring 3 times per month
history_present_illness: 57-year-old female with 6-year history of recurrent neurological episodes. Episodes include visual flickering, inability to speak or comprehend words, unilateral numbness, hemiparesis, and severe headaches lasting 3-7 days. Occurs approximately 3 times monthly. Strong family history of migraine. Previous workup for stroke was negative.
expected_diagnosis: Type 3 Hemiplegic Migraine (SCN1A gene mutation T1174S)
source: Frontiers in Neurology - Late onset type 3 hemiplegic migraine with permanent neurologic sequelae after attacks (2024)

symptoms.name: left-sided weakness
symptoms.description: Left upper limb power 2/5, bilateral lower limb power 2/5, right upper limb power 5/5

symptoms.name: dysarthria
symptoms.description: Deterioration in speech pattern, difficulty articulating words

symptoms.name: altered consciousness
symptoms.description: Glasgow Coma Scale declined from 15 to 5 within hours

chief_complaint: Acute onset of left-sided weakness, facial droop, and difficulty speaking
history_present_illness: 66-year-old male with history of COPD, atrial fibrillation, and previous stroke presents with sudden onset left-sided weakness and dysarthria. Patient currently diagnosed with COVID-19. Symptoms developed acutely, with progressive deterioration in consciousness (GCS 15→5). Exam shows left facial droop, left UE weakness (2/5), bilateral LE weakness (2/5), and respiratory distress.
expected_diagnosis: Right Frontal Cerebral Infarct (Acute Ischemic Stroke)
source: PMC7447108 - Clinical course of a 66-year-old man with an acute ischaemic stroke in the setting of a COVID-19 infection (2020)

symptoms.name: stumbling gait
symptoms.description: Tendency to fall, tandem gait mildly unstable

chief_complaint: Progressive neurological symptoms including gait instability, visual changes, extreme fatigue, and recent worsening of right-sided weakness
history_present_illness: 35-year-old female with long-standing neurological symptoms presents with progressive gait instability, visual disturbances, and severe fatigue over approximately 5 years. Recent acute worsening with right-sided hemisensory deficits and weakness (2 months duration). Additional symptoms include heat intolerance, bladder dysfunction, cognitive changes, and decreased hand dexterity. Currently on disease-modifying therapy.
source: University of Utah Medical Library - Multiple Sclerosis: Clinical Presentation Case 1

medical_history: Acute myelogenous leukemia (AML) at 18 months, treated with radiation and chemotherapy

symptoms.name: generalized tonic-clonic seizures
symptoms.description: Three seizures within hours - generalized body stiffening followed by left upper extremity elevation, left lower extremity straightening, rightward head turn, lasting ~3 minutes each

symptoms.name: urinary incontinence
symptoms.description: Loss of bladder control during seizure

symptoms.name: oxygen desaturation
symptoms.description: O2 saturation dropped to 67% during seizure

chief_complaint: Multiple generalized tonic-clonic seizures with first episode occurring earlier in the day, no prior seizure history
history_present_illness: 25-year-old female with history of childhood AML (treated with radiation and chemotherapy) presents with new-onset generalized tonic-clonic seizures. Patient experienced three seizures within several hours, each lasting approximately 3 minutes. Seizures characterized by generalized body stiffening, left arm elevation, left leg straightening, rightward head turning, urinary incontinence, and oxygen desaturation to 67%. Post-ictal confusion noted. No prior seizure history.
expected_diagnosis: New-Onset Generalized Tonic-Clonic Seizures secondary to Intracranial Meningioma

symptoms.name: resting tremor
symptoms.description: Intermittent resting tremor in left hand for 1 year

chief_complaint: One year of intermittent tremor in left hand that occurs primarily at rest
history_present_illness: 70-year-old male presents with 1-year history of intermittent resting tremor in left hand. Tremor is more noticeable when patient is relaxed and decreases with voluntary movement. Patient also reports mild slowing of movement and occasional stiffness. Neurological examination reveals mild asymmetrical bradykinesia and cogwheel rigidity. No significant prior neurological history.
source: PMC3002647 - Pharmacotherapy in Parkinson's disease: case studies (2010)
